problem_text:
A city planner is allocating funds for a municipal infrastructure upgrade across three fiscal years. They must select a portfolio of projects to maximize total community benefit while staying within the annual budget constraint.

The candidate projects are:
* Project A: cost 35 million, benefit 61 units
* Project B: cost 49 million, benefit 56 units
* Project C: cost 26 million, benefit 15 units
* Project D: cost 4 million, benefit 106 units
* Project E: cost 22 million, benefit 232 units
* Project F: cost 16 million, benefit 179 units
* Project G: cost 28 million, benefit 73 units
* Project H: cost 22 million, benefit 43 units
* Project I: cost 31 million, benefit 262 units
* Project J: cost 20 million, benefit 135 units
* Project K: cost 25 million, benefit 40 units
* Project L: cost 23 million, benefit 179 units
* Project M: cost 11 million, benefit 55 units
* Project N: cost 36 million, benefit 151 units
* Project O: cost 30 million, benefit 13 units
* Project P: cost 40 million, benefit 91 units
* Project Q: cost 10 million, benefit 295 units
* Project R: cost 37 million, benefit 182 units
* Project S: cost 44 million, benefit 242 units
* Project T: cost 45 million, benefit 44 units
* Project U: cost 25 million, benefit 149 units

Furthermore, due to mutually exclusive strategic considerations, exactly one of Project A and Project B must be approved.

If Project C is approved, it necessitates a separate, mandatory environmental mitigation fund, which reduces the effective available budget by 10 million.
The total budget allocation for the three-year period cannot exceed 405 million. The planner must determine the optimal set of projects to fund.
